review: 113.2c-1: the land_enters variant tested Soul Warden's creature-only trigger condition, not 113.2c; dropped it (and the Forest in hand it needed) and made one_warden the does_not_fire variant (a single instance yields no second trigger).
113.5-1: loyalty was left implicit though expected values depend on it; set Jace Beleren to 3 and Chandra Nalaar to 6 loyalty counters.
113.6a-1: decisions re-cast Lightning Bolt though setup already had it on the stack with Mountain tapped; decisions now start from that stack.

113.6e-1: Fog Patch costs {1}{G} but A had one Forest, so the castable variant could not pay; added a second Forest, marked Grizzly Bears not summoning sick, and made the attack declaration part of the setup.

113.6p-1: Gideon's loyalty was implicit; set 4 loyalty counters on it. The does_not_fire variant (no emblem made) is the only contrast the rule admits, since an emblem's ability cannot fail to function in the command zone.
113.7a-1: marked Karplusan Yeti not summoning sick in the zone entry; kept no_response as polarity other, because 113.7a admits no case where removing the source stops the ability.
113.9-1: reworded the Counterspell decision as an offer (it cannot be cast with no spell on the stack) and marked Prodigal Pyromancer not summoning sick.

113.10b-1: jump_after tested timestamp order (113.10c's scenario) and printed_only gave the same outcome as the base, so neither isolated 113.10b; replaced both with a no_removal does_not_fire variant.
113.11-1: noted that Archetype's own 'lose flying' clause also removes flying, so 113.11-2 is the isolating scenario.

113.12: triaged definitional, but it decides an observable continuous outcome (the rule's own Muraganda Petroglyphs example); reclassified as mechanical and added scenario 113.12-1 (Chaoslace vs Jump under Muraganda Petroglyphs).

skipped.reason: no card in Forge's cardsfolder has an ability that states zones it does not function in (Oracle text searched), so the situation cannot be built

scenarios.title: Two instances of the same triggered ability each trigger independently

setup.notes: Soul Warden reads: whenever another creature enters, you gain 1 life. Both Soul Wardens have been on the battlefield since a previous turn.

decisions: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest and Forest.
Both players pass; Grizzly Bears resolves and enters the battlefield.
Each Soul Warden's trigger is put on the stack; both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: two_wardens
variants.expected: Two separate Soul Warden triggers go on the stack and each resolves; A gains 1 life twice and ends at 22 life.

variants.label: one_warden
variants.delta: A controls only one Soul Warden.
variants.expected: One Soul Warden trigger resolves; A ends at 21 life.

scenarios.title: A planeswalker's second loyalty ability in a turn is not playable

setup.notes: Both planeswalkers have been under A's control since a previous turn. Each library holds at least 10 cards. The stack is empty.

decisions: A activates Jace Beleren's +2 (each player draws a card); both players pass and it resolves.
With the stack empty in the same main phase, A is offered a second loyalty ability: first Jace Beleren's -1 targeting B.

variants.label: same_permanent
variants.expected: Jace Beleren has 5 loyalty and A and B each drew a card. Activating Jace Beleren's -1 is not playable (a loyalty ability of that permanent was already activated this turn).

variants.label: other_permanent
variants.delta: The second activation offered is Chandra Nalaar's +1 targeting B instead.
variants.expected: Chandra Nalaar's +1 is playable (no loyalty ability of Chandra Nalaar was activated this turn); it resolves, Chandra Nalaar has 7 loyalty and B has 19 life.

scenarios.title: A characteristic-defining ability applies in the hand

setup.notes: A controls no lands. Transguild Courier is all colors by a characteristic-defining ability, so it is a blue card while in A's hand.

decisions: Lightning Bolt (cast by B, Mountain already tapped) is on the stack targeting A; B passes priority and A receives priority.
A is offered Force of Will targeting Lightning Bolt, paying its alternative cost (1 life and exile a blue card from hand).

variants.label: courier_in_hand
variants.expected: Force of Will is castable: Transguild Courier is a blue card, so exiling it and paying 1 life pays the alternative cost (cost after adjustment is 1 life plus exiling Transguild Courier).

variants.label: green_card_in_hand
variants.delta: The second card in A's hand is Grizzly Bears (green) instead of Transguild Courier.
variants.expected: Force of Will is not castable: A has no blue card to exile and no mana for its mana cost.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge applies Transguild Courier's SetColor static as a characteristic-defining ability (CharacteristicDefining$ True), which is what makes it blue in the hand.

scenarios.title: A graveyard-only trigger works from the graveyard and not from the hand
decisions: A plays Swamp as a land drop.
If Bloodghast's landfall trigger is put on the stack, A chooses to return it; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: in_graveyard
variants.expected: Bloodghast's landfall trigger fires from the graveyard and, on resolution, Bloodghast moves from the graveyard to the battlefield.

variants.label: in_hand
variants.delta: Bloodghast is in A's hand instead of A's graveyard.
variants.expected: Bloodghast's landfall ability does not function in the hand: no trigger fires and Bloodghast stays in A's hand.

scenarios.title: An alternative cost of a spell can be paid when casting it

setup.notes: Fireblast's mana cost is {4}{R}{R}; A has only two lands.

decisions: A casts Fireblast targeting B, paying the alternative cost: sacrifice Mountain and Mountain.
Both players pass; Fireblast resolves.

variants.label: two_mountains
variants.expected: Fireblast is castable for its alternative cost with no mana: both Mountains are sacrificed and B takes 4 damage (16 life).

variants.label: one_mountain
variants.delta: A controls only one Mountain.
variants.expected: Fireblast is not castable: the alternative cost (sacrifice two Mountains) cannot be paid and neither can the {4}{R}{R} mana cost.

scenarios.title: A cost-modifying ability of a spell applies while it is cast

setup.notes: Craw Wurm is 6/4 and Earth Elemental is 4/5. Ghalta's mana cost is {10}{G}{G} and it costs {X} less, X being the total power of creatures A controls.

decisions: A casts Ghalta, Primal Hunger, tapping Forest and Forest.
Both players pass; Ghalta resolves.

variants.label: power_ten
variants.expected: Total power is 10, so the cost after adjustment is {G}{G}; Ghalta is castable and enters the battlefield.

variants.label: power_eight
variants.delta: Earth Elemental is replaced by Grizzly Bears (power 2).
variants.expected: Total power is 8, so the cost after adjustment is {2}{G}{G}; with two Forests Ghalta is not castable.

scenarios.title: A casting-timing restriction on a spell applies to it in hand

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears has been under A's control since a previous turn and is attacking B. B controls no creatures. The stack is empty and A has priority.

decisions: A has declared Grizzly Bears as an attacker.
A, with priority, is offered Fog Patch (cast only during the declare blockers step), tapping Forest and Forest.

variants.label: declare_attackers_step
variants.expected: Fog Patch is not castable in the declare attackers step.

variants.label: declare_blockers_step
variants.delta: B has declared no blockers and A has priority in the declare blockers step instead (setup step declare_blockers).
variants.expected: Fog Patch is castable; it resolves and Grizzly Bears becomes blocked.

scenarios.title: A cast-from-exile permission applies in exile only
decisions: A casts Misthollow Griffin, tapping four Islands.
Both players pass; Misthollow Griffin resolves.

variants.label: in_exile
variants.expected: Misthollow Griffin is castable from exile; it resolves and enters the battlefield.

variants.label: in_graveyard
variants.delta: Misthollow Griffin is in A's graveyard instead of exile.
variants.expected: Misthollow Griffin is not castable from the graveyard.

scenarios.title: A spell that can't be countered resolves despite a counterspell
decisions: A casts Abrupt Decay targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Swamp and Forest.
B casts Counterspell targeting Abrupt Decay, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: abrupt_decay
variants.expected: Counterspell resolves but does not counter Abrupt Decay; Abrupt Decay resolves and Grizzly Bears moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: doom_blade
variants.delta: A casts Doom Blade targeting Grizzly Bears (tapping Swamp and Forest) instead of Abrupt Decay.
variants.expected: Counterspell counters Doom Blade, which moves to A's graveyard; Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.title: An enters-tapped ability applies as the permanent enters
decisions: A casts Diregraf Ghoul, tapping Swamp.
Both players pass; Diregraf Ghoul resolves.

variants.label: diregraf_ghoul
variants.expected: Diregraf Ghoul enters the battlefield tapped (the replacement effect modifies the entry itself; it is never untapped on the battlefield).

variants.label: grizzly_bears
variants.delta: A casts Grizzly Bears, tapping Forest and Forest, instead of Diregraf Ghoul.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears enters the battlefield untapped.

scenarios.title: A permanent that can't have counters put on it gets none
decisions: A casts Dragonscale Boon targeting Melira's Keepers, tapping four Forests.
Both players pass; Dragonscale Boon resolves.

variants.label: keepers_target
variants.expected: No counters are put on Melira's Keepers, which stays 4/4 with no counters.

variants.label: bears_target
variants.delta: Dragonscale Boon targets Grizzly Bears instead.
variants.expected: Two +1/+1 counters are put on Grizzly Bears, which is 4/4.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's CantPutCounter static for Melira's Keepers is limited to Card.Self+inZoneBattlefield, so the 'as it enters' half of the rule is not illustrated.

scenarios.title: Cycling works from the hand because its discard cost can't be paid on the battlefield

setup.notes: Each library holds at least 10 cards.

decisions: A is offered Barkhide Mauler's cycling ability (cost: {2}, discard Barkhide Mauler), tapping Forest and Forest.

variants.label: in_hand
variants.expected: Cycling is playable from the hand: Barkhide Mauler is discarded to A's graveyard and A draws a card.

variants.label: on_battlefield
variants.delta: Barkhide Mauler is on the battlefield instead of A's hand.
variants.expected: Cycling is not playable: its cost (discard this card) cannot be paid from the battlefield.

variants.label: in_graveyard
variants.delta: Barkhide Mauler is in A's graveyard instead of A's hand.
variants.expected: Cycling is not playable from the graveyard: the card cannot be discarded from there.

scenarios.title: A cycling trigger fires from the graveyard where the cycled card sits

setup.notes: A's library holds at least 10 cards. Goblin Piker and Raging Goblin are the only Goblins on the battlefield.

decisions: A cycles Gempalm Incinerator, tapping both Mountains.
Gempalm Incinerator's cycling trigger is put on the stack targeting Grizzly Bears; A chooses to have it deal damage; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: cycled
variants.expected: The cycling trigger fires from the graveyard; X is 2 (two Goblins on the battlefield), so Gempalm Incinerator deals 2 damage to Grizzly Bears, which moves to B's graveyard.

variants.label: discarded
variants.delta: A casts Tormenting Voice (tapping both Mountains) discarding Gempalm Incinerator instead of cycling it.
variants.expected: Gempalm Incinerator is discarded, not cycled: no trigger fires and Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield undamaged.

scenarios.title: A return-from-graveyard ability is activatable only from the graveyard
decisions: A is offered Reassembling Skeleton's ability ({1}{B}: return it from your graveyard to the battlefield tapped), tapping Swamp and Swamp.

variants.label: in_graveyard
variants.expected: The ability is playable; on resolution Reassembling Skeleton moves from the graveyard to the battlefield tapped.

variants.label: on_battlefield
variants.delta: Reassembling Skeleton is on the battlefield instead of A's graveyard.
variants.expected: The ability is not playable: it functions only in the graveyard.

variants.label: in_hand
variants.delta: Reassembling Skeleton is in A's hand instead of A's graveyard.
variants.expected: The ability is not playable from the hand.

scenarios.title: An emblem's static ability functions in the command zone

setup.notes: Gideon, Ally of Zendikar has its starting loyalty of 4 and has not been activated this turn.

decisions: A activates Gideon's -4: A gets an emblem with 'Creatures you control get +1/+1.'
Both players pass; the ability resolves.

variants.label: emblem
variants.expected: A has the emblem in the command zone; Gideon has 0 loyalty and moves to A's graveyard, yet Grizzly Bears is 3/3. Hill Giant stays 3/3.

variants.label: knight_token
variants.delta: A activates Gideon's 0 (create a 2/2 Knight Ally token) instead.
variants.expected: No emblem is created; Grizzly Bears stays 2/2, A has a 2/2 Knight Ally token, and Gideon stays on the battlefield with 4 loyalty.

scenarios.title: An activated ability on the stack resolves after its source is gone

setup.notes: Karplusan Yeti is 3/3 and has been under A's control since a previous turn.

decisions: A activates Karplusan Yeti's ability ({T}) targeting Hill Giant.
B, with the ability on the stack, casts Lightning Bolt targeting Karplusan Yeti, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: source_killed
variants.expected: Lightning Bolt resolves first and Karplusan Yeti dies; the ability then still resolves using the Yeti's last known power of 3: Hill Giant is dealt 3 damage and dies, and the Yeti (already gone) takes no damage back.

variants.label: no_response
variants.delta: B does not cast Lightning Bolt.
variants.expected: The ability resolves with the Yeti on the battlefield: Hill Giant is dealt 3 damage and the Yeti is dealt 3 damage in return; both die.

scenarios.title: A spell-only counterspell can't counter an ability, while an ability counterspell can

setup.notes: Prodigal Pyromancer has been under A's control since a previous turn.

decisions: A activates Prodigal Pyromancer's ability ({T}) targeting B.
B, with the ability on the stack and no spell on the stack, is offered Counterspell targeting the ability, tapping two Islands.
Both players pass until the stack is empty.

variants.label: counterspell
variants.expected: Counterspell can't target the ability (it is not a spell), so it is not castable; the ability resolves and B has 19 life.

variants.label: stifle
variants.delta: B casts Stifle (tapping one Island) targeting the ability instead of Counterspell.
variants.expected: Stifle counters the ability; it doesn't resolve and B stays at 20 life.

scenarios.title: Removing an ability removes every instance of it

setup.notes: Wind Drake has flying printed on it.

decisions: A casts Jump targeting Wind Drake, tapping Island; Jump resolves (a second instance of flying until end of turn).
A casts Turn to Frog targeting Wind Drake, tapping Island and Island; Turn to Frog resolves.

variants.label: two_instances
variants.expected: Wind Drake is a 1/1 blue Frog with no flying: both its printed flying and the flying from Jump were removed.

variants.label: no_removal
variants.delta: A does not cast Turn to Frog.
variants.expected: Wind Drake is a 2/2 Drake with flying (its printed instance and Jump's instance).

scenarios.title: When effects add and remove the same ability, the most recent prevails
decisions: A casts Turn to Frog targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island and Island; Turn to Frog resolves.
A casts Jump targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island; Jump resolves.

variants.label: add_last
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a 1/1 blue Frog with flying: the later effect (Jump) prevails over the earlier removal.

variants.label: remove_last
variants.delta: A casts Jump first and then Turn to Frog.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is a 1/1 blue Frog with no flying: the later effect (Turn to Frog) prevails.

scenarios.title: An object that can't have an ability loses it

setup.notes: Wind Drake has flying printed on it.

decisions: No decisions are needed; the board is stable.

variants.label: opponents_creature
variants.expected: Wind Drake has no flying; Archetype of Imagination has flying.

variants.label: own_creature
variants.delta: B controls Archetype of Imagination instead of A.
variants.expected: Wind Drake has flying.

scenarios.forge_notes: Archetype of Imagination also says opponents' creatures lose flying, so this scenario shows the loss jointly with that clause; 113.11-2 isolates the can't-have clause.

scenarios.title: An object that can't have an ability can't gain it
decisions: B casts Jump targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island.
Both players pass; Jump resolves.

variants.label: archetype_present
variants.expected: Jump resolves but Grizzly Bears does not gain flying.

variants.label: archetype_absent
variants.delta: Archetype of Imagination is in A's graveyard instead of on the battlefield.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears gains flying until end of turn.

scenarios.title: An effect that sets a color is not an ability, while a granted keyword is

setup.notes: Grizzly Bears has no abilities, so Muraganda Petroglyphs makes it 4/4 before anything is cast.

decisions: A casts Chaoslace targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Chaoslace resolves.

variants.label: becomes_red
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears is red and still has no abilities, so it stays 4/4.

variants.label: gains_flying
variants.delta: A casts Jump targeting Grizzly Bears, tapping Island, instead of Chaoslace.
variants.expected: Grizzly Bears gains flying, now has an ability, and is 2/2.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge implements Chaoslace as an Animate effect with only Colors$; check that Creature.NoAbilities still matches after it.
